correctness.rationale: At every integer Cayley order k>=2, on the specified symmetric translation-invariant branch z=t of the zero-field source model, the equation P(s)=c1 s^(k+1)-c2 s^k+s-1=0 holds for s>0 and arbitrary positive coefficients c1,c2 realizable by source real parameters. Rearranging to c2=q(s)=c1 s+(s-1)/s^k makes q prime have the sign of the strictly convex H(s)=c1 s^(k+1)-(k-1)s+k. The minimum is nonnegative iff c1>=((k-1)/(k+1))^(k+1), forcing one root for every c2>0. Subcritical H has exactly two roots s_-<s_+, yielding two positive distinct fold levels c2lo<c2hi, exactly 3 simple positive roots between, 2 distinct roots with one double at folds, and 1 root otherwise. At critical coefficients (rho^(k+1),rho^(k-1)), s=1/rho is one triple root with P=P'=P''=0, P'''=k(k-1)rho^2>0. Independent exact symbolic differentiation using SymPy verified cusp derivatives for k=2,3,4,5,6,10,20. All-k classification rests on the convexity proof, not bounded checking. No nonsymmetric root count or physical dominance is proved.

Critically, FULL older Ganikhodjaev–Idris (2013) seven-page paper was independently inspected: it already gives a k=2 simple BEG exact three/two/one-solution interval and fold geometry for its particular physical subfamily (Lemma 1, eqs.10–13), so k=2 phase coexistence is prior work and must be credited. That older result does not imply the complete all-k, all-positive-coefficient parameterization here. General cubic cusp calculus is routine background, but the specific sourced higher-k global diagram resolves an open upper-bound ambiguity; no dominating source located by published Resultary search.
